messages:
Maria J: rolling up a new embedding candidate (vega-emb-v2) for production — running noise-sensitivity and UMAP stability checks. can folks quick-scan the smallholdout results? need to decide if we proceed to int8 quantize step. :thinking:
Aj Patel: sending the small-run now. dataset = internal-qa-5k holdout, seed=42. baseline=open-embed-1 (fp16), candidate=vega-emb-v2 (fp16). quick numbers:
```
# recall@1, recall@5, recall@10
open-embed-1: 0.642, 0.812, 0.867
vega-emb-v2: 0.635, 0.800, 0.860
vega-emb-v2 + gaussian noise eps=1e-3: 0.600, 0.770, 0.830
```
Devin K: hmm ~2% absolute drop at recall@1 and a bigger sensitivity to tiny Gaussian noise. did you normalize with L2 before similarity?
Aj Patel: yes L2ed. also tried dropout-like token masking during embed step (10% tokens) — similar fragility. full command I ran:
```
python eval/embeddings_eval.py --model vega-emb-v2 --dataset internal-qa-5k --metric recall@10 --seed 42 --noise_eps 0.001
```
Simon L: can you paste the UMAP plots? I'm curious if clusters shift wholesale or if a few classes collapse. :eyes:
Aj Patel: uploading quick PNGs to the run artifact (link: https://artifacts/redwood/vega-v2/1845012345). UMAP shows that two domain clusters (billing vs infra) get closer under noise, but others stable.
EvalBot: automated summary: run_id=1845012345-vegav2-smallholdout, recall@1_drop=0.007, recall@10_drop=0.007, noise_sensitivity_score=0.12 (higher is worse).
Maria J: thanks. initial instinct: baseline more robust. but vega has slightly better cluster compactness in float, and smaller dims (512 vs 1024) which is attractive for cost. need to know quantized behavior before deciding.
Devin K: request: run 3 seeds (23, 42, 99) and both fp16 vs int8-quantized via our q4f pipeline. include adversarial noise test (swap 1 token with random token) and report recall@k variance across seeds. also add silhouette score and per-class recall delta.
Aj Patel: ack. kicking off multi-seed runs now via k8s job: `k8s run eval-embed-vega-multiseed --seeds 23,42,99 --quant int8,fp16 --noise gaussian,adv` ETA ~1h.
Simon L: FYI earlier int8 runs on other models showed ~3-4% recall@1 drop but stable recall@10. watch for per-class hits — infra-related queries are brittle historically.
Maria J: action items: 1) Aj: post full table of per-class recall deltas and silhouette numbers when done. 2) Devin: script to compute recall variance and p-value between baseline and candidate. 3) Simon: review artifact UMAPs for int8 results and flag any domain collapse. We'll reconvene after results. :thumbsup:
Aj Patel: noted — I'll include the train/holdout sample of 200 queries that flip across top-1 for manual inspection. will paste CSV snippet here once ready.
EvalBot: job started: job_id=job-embed-vega-1845012301, tracking: https://jobs.redwood/job-embed-vega-1845012301
Devin K: quick thought — also compare cosine vs dot-product after quantization; quant rounding can change magnitude distribution and affect cosine after L2. small check saves headaches.
Maria J: good call. add that to job config. thanks team, will watch the artifacts.
